topics.title: Reserving
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to apply valuation principles for short duration group and health insurance contracts.

outcomes.text: Describe the types of claim reserves
Explain the limitations and biases of the traditional valuation methods
Calculate appropriate claim reserves given data
Describe, calculate, and evaluate the impact of environmental factors on reserve calculations (trend, seasonality, claims processing changes, etc.)
Evaluate data resources and appropriateness for calculating reserves
Describe, calculate, and evaluate non-IBNR types of reserves and explain when each is required
Apply applicable best practices related to reserving

topics.title: Financial Statements
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to prepare and interpret insurance company financial statements in accordance with Statutory Accounting Standards and GAAP.

outcomes.text: Prepare a financial statement in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
Interpret the results of both statutory and GAAP statements from the viewpoint of stakeholders, including regulators, senior management, and investors
Project financial outcomes and recommend strategy
Evaluate capital needs using RBC and the use of reinsurance to mitigate capital strain
Apply applicable best practices related to financial statements

topics.title: Flow of Funds
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to describe the flow of funds in the health care system and the role of providers in the system.

outcomes.text: Establish a framework of how funds flow through the health care system
Describe the role physicians play and their influence on the flow of funds
Describe the market power of hospitals and how provider systems compete for patients, physicians, and contracts
Describe the flow of funds in the Canadian healthcare system and the roles of the provider and government
